articles.title: In 2025, researchers explored the USS Yorktown wreck three miles below the Pacific; inside its hangar sat what may be a 1941 Ford station wagon
articles.summary: In April 2025, a NOAA exploration team discovered a 1940s Ford station wagon inside the wreck of the USS Yorktown, unveiling mysteries of WWII as they investigated the iconic aircraft carrier sunk during the Battle of Midway.
articles.body: One of the most well-known of them is the aircraft carrier USS Yorktown, which fought in the Coral Sea and Midway before going missing in the middle of the Pacific in June 1942. Her specific location of repose was unclear for decades afterward. In 1998, a US Navy and National Geographic expedition discovered the shipwreck about 1,000 miles northwest of Honolulu, according to NOAA. In April 2025 a crew from NOAA Ocean Exploration came back with a more ambitious plan: to look inside the ship’s hangar for the first time.The cameras revealed several unexpected discoveries. Down on the aft hangar deck, more than three miles below the surface, lay a black Ford station wagon, about 1940 or 1941. No human divers approached it. The exploration was carried out by the remotely operated vehicle Deep Discoverer, and the car has since become the most talked about discovery from the dives.How the dives operatedThe dives occurred on April 19 and 20, 2025, as part of NOAA’s Papahānaumokuākea ROV and Mapping expedition aboard the research vessel Okeanos Explorer. Pilots from the Global Foundation for Ocean Exploration carefully guided Deep Discoverer through the No. 3 elevator shaft and into the hangar, avoiding entanglement hazards. The team emphasised that it did not disturb the wreck.Inside, the vehicle found a hand-painted mural, A Chart of the Cruises of the USS Yorktown, a world map about 42 feet wide, depicting the carrier’s journeys. It also located at least three Douglas SBD Dauntless dive bombers. One was upside down with a 500-pound bomb still in its cradle. Another was marked with the insignia of a plane from the U.S.S. Enterprise, which had landed at Yorktown after striking the Japanese carrier Kaga. NOAA says it’s the first time aircraft that fought at Midway have been located on the battlefield proper.The car mysteryThe first clue came on 19 April when, looking into the hangar from the port side, the team saw a faint shape of a car. The next day, experts could get a better look at its features, and NOAA Ocean Exploration says they provisionally identified it as a black 1941 Ford Super Deluxe Woody. The giveaways were a split windshield, a canvas top, a chrome bumper, rectangular rear windows and a spare tire on the back.Part of the front plate is visible. The top line says ship service. The bottom is tougher to see; it might have the ship's hull number or just mention US NAVY. NOAA researchers hypothesized that the automobile may have been used by senior officers or other crew members while the carrier was conducting business in foreign ports.The situation poses unpleasant questions. Yorktown spent only about 48 hours in repairs at Pearl Harbor before going for Midway, and her officers knew a battle was impending. If the sailors ejected guns and planes when they worked to right the ship's list, why was the automobile kept? The NOAA team wonders whether it had special meaning for the crew and officers hoping to preserve the ship. Nobody has an answer yet.Protecting a war graveOn the morning of June 7, 1942, as she was being towed back towards Pearl Harbor, two torpedoes from a Japanese submarine struck Yorktown, and she sank. Commissioned in 1937, she was about 809 feet long and could transport about 2,200 people and 90 aircraft. It is the final burial place of many servicemen, and in 2023 the US Navy declared it a Site of Extraordinary Character.The Naval History and Heritage Command lists USS Yorktown as a Site of Extraordinary Character and says full-scale permits for activities that would disturb such sites will be denied. That is why cameras, not salvage crews, are the tools of choice.In April 2025, more than three miles below the surface, a robot found a black wood-bodied Ford in the USS Yorktown’s hangar. It’s presumably a 1940 or 1941 Super Deluxe; it looks to have been the Navy’s, and we’re still puzzled as to why it survived on board during the Battle of Midway.You use AI every day. articles.title: Game of one-upmanship? For fourth day in a row, INDIA bloc MPs hit the streets ahead of CJP's Jantar Mantar 2.0
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: For four days in a row, opposition leaders have hit the streets of the national capital, demanding removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged
articles.body: NEW DELHI: For four days in a row, opposition leaders have hit the streets of the national capital, demanding removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the SIR of electoral rolls. On September 30, when the INDIA bloc announced its 6-point protest plan against the CEC, it mentioned one street protest in the national capital - a march by all its MPs to the EC office on October 6.But the script changed.The opposition MPs, led by the Congress, returned to the streets with a march to Jantar Mantar on October 7, to Rajghat on October 8 and to Rashtrapati Bhawan on October 9. The police went all out to stop the protesters on October 7 leading to a 9-hour standoff at Akashvani Bhawan where Rahul and Priyanka sat on a dharna, before they were forcibly removed. However, a day later the cops changed their strategy and allowed the opposition leaders led by Rahul Gandhi to offer prayers at Rajghat, Mahatma Gandhi's memorial. The leaders staged a sit-in to highlight what they alleged was "hijacking" of the country by Prime Minister Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and the CEC through a criminal conspiracy of "vote chori."On Friday, on the eve of CJP protests, the INDIA bloc MPs once again took to the streets, this time to Rashtrapati Bhawan to submit a memorandum to President Droupadi Murmu. The march, as expected, was stopped by the cops. The opposition leaders then sat on a dharna, this time at Vijay Chowk.The change in the street protests plan took even some of the INDIA bloc allies by surprise with some reports suggesting that allies were not happy over not being consulted. Not all of them were present for the extended street protests, leading to some uncomfortable questions about the INDIA bloc’s unity. Congress denied these charges.Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said all parties of the INDIA bloc had been invited, but the decision and communication came late on Tuesday night. "Therefore, it was natural that representatives from some parties could not participate in it. Some media outlets are making unnecessary comments about this," he posted on X.So, what prompted this change in protest plan? Was it the success of the October 6 march to Parliament protest that prompted the new strategy? Or, did the looming Cockroach Janata Party’s October 10 protest play a role in extending the INDIA bloc street action?To understand this, let’s rewind to June-July when youth came out in large numbers in several cities in response to the CJP’s agitation demanding the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union education minister against NEET paper leaks.The CJP, formed online in May by Abhijeet Dipke in response to a remark made by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant using terms "cockroaches" and "parasites" for those unemployed who attacked institutions through social media activism and litigation.On June 1, Dipke announced the first CJP protest for June 6 at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi. The next day, activist and educator Sonam Wangchuk joined the online movement. On June 6, the CJP launched physical demonstrations at Jantar Mantar. On 28 June 2026, Wangchuk joined the demonstration at Jantar Mantar and started an indefinite hunger strike demanding the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan.The agitation peaked on July 20, when students and youth from across the country marched to Jantar Mantar responding to CJP’s call. The Delhi police resorted to using unprecedented force to disperse the protesters. The political parties, which till then stood on the sidelines, tried to enter the protests. The Congress, which had focused on Rahul Gandhi’s “Chhatron ki Goonj” till then, staged a surprise protest outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s residence on July 21 to make its presence felt on the streets. However, the fulcrum of the anti-NEET paper leak protests remained the CJP, and the government was forced to accept its demand for resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan.With another CJP buildup in the making, the opposition parties led by the Congress perhaps don’t want to be “missing in action” this time around and leave the field open for the CJP. That could be one of the reasons why the INDIA bloc MPs have extended their stay on the streets.The Delhi Police have denied permission to the CJP for the October 10 Jantar Mantar protests citing short notice, past non-compliance with directions and concerns related to public safety, law and order and traffic regulation.But the CJP has announced to go ahead with its agitation. Abhijeet Dipke asserted that the protest would go ahead regardless of whether police permission was granted and said CJP activists were prepared to face arrest.Questioning the measures taken ahead of the protest, Dipke said, "What is this fear? Why are you this scared? You are scared of the youth in the country. You shut down trains, you shut down Metro, what should one do?"Earlier today, Delhi Police announced an unprecedented security clampdown on the national capital to prevent protesters from assembling for the agitation. The cops are also keeping an eye on over 200 content creators as part of the monitoring exercise. Police teams are examining online posts and messages relating to mobilisation, gathering points and the proposed demonstration.Later in the day, Supreme Court intervened and ordered Delhi police to ease some of the sweeping instructions to ensure that citizens, particularly those who have no intention of joining the ongoing demonstrations, were not inconvenienced. The top court said Metro and train services cannot be completely stopped and asked authorities to reconsider such restrictions in a proportionate manner.A bench led by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also clarified that the present proceedings primarily concern restrictions affecting the movement of ordinary citizens and public transport and not the broader right to protest.While the government and security forces will be closely watching the CJP's mobilisation on Saturday, the INDIA bloc will also be keeping an eagle's eye on how the youth respond. In July, the CJP managed to draw large crowds, leaving opposition parties struggling to make their presence felt.This time, the opposition has taken to the streets even before the CJP's planned protest. The question now is whether the INDIA bloc can match the CJP's mobilisation or whether the youth-led group will once again draw bigger crowds. The October 10 protest at Jantar Mantar may offer some answers.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: US impose sanctions on ICC with threat to 'end' international court
articles.summary: The US says the measures are aimed at restricting the tribunal's resources and ability to operate.
articles.body:
The Trump administration has imposed sweeping sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC), saying it wants to restrict the tribunal's resources and ability to operate.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the measures - which include a ban on US entities making transactions with the ICC - were intended to "defend US sovereignty" and accused the court of seeking to prosecute Americans.

The ICC said the measures were an assault on the rule of law and the foundations of the international legal order.

The announcement comes just hours after former ICC judge Navi Pillay was awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her efforts to promote peace and international law.

US President Donald Trump has reacted sourly to the Norwegian prize's choice of winner this year and last, after having expressed a desire to receive it himself. He criticised Pillay for being part of a panel that accused Israel, as well as Hamas, of war crimes during the 7 October conflict.

The US says the ICC has no jurisdiction over it as it never ratified the statute founding it - but the international court has investigated US actions elsewhere.

Rubio said Trump would not allow the ICC to prosecute Americans, adding: "Either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC."

The US sanctions will stop US companies from providing goods or services to the ICC, such as banking or software.

Rubio said Washington had delayed imposing the sanctions in the hope that the ICC and its member countries would address US concerns. He said the measures had been structured to allow other countries to negotiate a possible solution.

He also called on US allies that were ICC signatories to "rein in" the institution.

The ICC responded by saying that the sanctions were aimed at disrupting its work and intimidating those who co-operate with it - but that it "will not be deterred".

The Trump administration has repeatedly criticised the court, including over its investigation into the actions of US forces in Afghanistan, a probe it has since deprioritised.

It has also been critical of the ICC issuing arrest warrants for Israeli officials including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
